entry.evidence: The radical observations in PRD, where the cities are suffering from severe O 3 pollution, have not been conducted since 2014

steps.action: Cite the OH underestimation repeatedly found by other campaigns in low-NO, high-VOC environments.
steps.quote: The underestimation of OH radicals in environments characterized by low NO and high volatile organic compounds (VOCs) has been identified

steps.action: Cite the proposed rival OH-regeneration mechanisms, the Leuven isoprene mechanism (LIM) and the X mechanism, and note that LIM is insufficient and the nature of X unknown.
steps.quote: New radical mechanisms involving unclassical OH regeneration have been proposed, mainly including Leuven isoprene mechanism (LIM) and X mechanism

steps.action: Pose the aims: radical levels and model closure in PRD after a gap since 2014, missing OH sources, ROx budget and atmospheric oxidation capacity.
steps.quote: The radical observations in PRD, where the cities are suffering from severe O 3 pollution, have not been conducted since 2014

steps.action: Run the STORM field campaign at an urban Shenzhen site in September to October 2018, where ambient conditions are found rather than set.
steps.quote: The STORM campaign was conducted from September to October 2018 in Peking University Shenzhen Graduate School

steps.action: Measure meteorology, photolysis frequencies, OH reactivity (LP-LIF), trace gases, VOCs (GC-MS), HONO and HCHO to constrain the radical chemistry.
steps.quote: a comprehensive set of trace gases was conducted to support the exploration of radical chemistry

steps.action: Cross-check the inorganic trace gases with two independent sets of instruments; they agree within uncertainty.
steps.quote: were simultaneously measured by two sets of instruments, and good agreement was achieved within the uncertainty

steps.action: After the OH reference cell failed, use the HO2 cell for wavelength reference at higher NO, calibrate the HO2-to-OH conversion (80-95% low-NO, 100% high-NO), and keep only high-NO data as HO2* including RO2 interference.
steps.quote: Owing to the failure of the reference cell in this campaign

steps.action: Check for OH measurement interference: cite pre-injector tests from earlier campaigns, compare Shenzhen conditions with Wangdu, and add ROOOH chemistry to the model, finding no correlation with the OH model-observation discrepancy.
steps.quote: the OH interference during this campaign was negligible according to the analysis of the behavior of the PKU-LIF system in previous campaigns

steps.action: Set up the observation-constrained zero-dimensional box model RACM2-LIM1 (5 min resolution, 2 d spin-up) to compute expected radical concentrations.
steps.quote: we conducted the radical closure experiment based on the Regional Atmospheric Chemistry Mechanism updated with the latest isoprene chemistry (RACM2-LIM1)

steps.action: Design two closure tests: modeled versus observed concentrations, and an OH experimental budget in which destruction (observed OH times kOH) minus known production gives the missing source.
steps.quote: there are two types of radical closure experiment

steps.action: Report the observed conditions (Fig. 2) and the OH and HO2* time series and daily maxima over 5-28 October.
steps.quote: The daily maxima of the observed OH and HO 2 * concentrations varied

steps.action: Compare observed and modeled OH diurnal profiles: they agree within uncertainty overall, but OH is systematically underestimated after 10:00 CST as NO falls.
steps.quote: a systematic difference existed, with the observed OH concentration being about 1 × 10 6 cm - 3 higher than the modeled OH concentration

steps.action: Estimate the RO2 interference in HO2* as the difference between modeled HO2* and HO2, using RO2 sensitivities from Lu et al. (2012): 23-28% in daytime.
steps.quote: It ranged within 23 %–28 % during the daytime

steps.action: Compare observed and modeled HO2*: the model overestimates the observations.
steps.quote: The observed HO 2 * was overestimated by the model

steps.action: Propose heterogeneous HO2 uptake on aerosol as the missing HO2 sink.
steps.quote: indicating the HO 2 heterogeneous uptake might have a significant impact during this campaign

steps.action: Check the modeled kOH against kOH measured on 5-19 October; they agree within uncertainty, which justifies using modeled kOH for the whole campaign.
steps.quote: A good agreement between the observed k OH and modeled k OH within the uncertainties was achieved

steps.action: Compare OH destruction and known production rates: a gap of 3.1-4.6 ppb/h at midday, beyond combined uncertainties, is a missing OH source (a lower limit because HO2* was used).
steps.quote: cannot be explained by the combined experimental uncertainties

steps.action: Bin OH and HO2* observations and simulations, and VOC reactivity speciation, by NO concentration: the OH underestimation grows toward low NO, where isoprene and OVOC reactivity are larger.
steps.quote: a continuously increasing underestimation of the observed OH was found towards lower NO concentrations

steps.action: Take up the X mechanism of Hofzumahaus et al. (2009) and the X amounts fitted at other Chinese sites.
steps.quote: Hofzumahaus et al. (2009) proposed an existence of a pathway for the regeneration of OH independent of NO

steps.action: Fit a constant X mixing ratio in the base model to reproduce observed OH: 0.1 ppb X gives agreement, including at low NO (Fig. 5).
steps.quote: Good agreement between observations and simulations of OH radicals was achieved when a constant mixing ratio of 0.1 ppb of X

steps.action: Keep unclassical OH recycling as the explanation, noting that the nature of X is unknown.
steps.quote: Unclassical OH recycling was identified again in this study.

steps.action: Compare the required X with Backgarden and Heshan (higher) and attribute the difference to air masses and VOC reactivity composition.
steps.quote: the required X concentration at the Backgarden and Heshan sites in PRD was higher

steps.action: Compute the OH production that the LIM1 isoprene isomerization mechanism contributes against the missing source.
steps.quote: Herein, we evaluated the contribution of the LIM1 mechanism to the missing OH sources

steps.action: Reject LIM1 as a sufficient explanation: it explains about 7% of the missing OH source.
steps.quote: The LIM1 mechanism can explain approximately 7 % of the missing OH sources during 10:00–16:00 CST

steps.action: Run modified MACR and MVK oxidation schemes (H-migration and HO2 reactions after Fuchs et al.) to compute their OH regeneration.
steps.quote: the impacts of MACR and MVK oxidation were evaluated here

steps.action: Reject MACR and MVK chemistry (no significant contribution, Fig. S5) and conclude that isoprene chemistry leaves most of the missing OH unexplained.
steps.quote: a large part of missing OH sources was not explained by the isoprene chemistry

steps.action: Add HO2 uptake to RACM2-LIM1 (ASA from PM2.5 times 20) and run sensitivity experiments with literature gamma values 0.08 and 0.2.
steps.quote: we coupled HO 2 heterogeneous uptake into the base model (RACM2-LIM1) and conducted three sensitivity experiments

steps.action: Compare these runs with observed HO2*: gamma 0.08 and 0.2 do not match.
steps.quote: The modeled HO 2 * cannot match well with the observations when a γ value of 0.08 and 0.2 was set in the model.

steps.action: Raise gamma to about 0.3, which matches observed HO2* and lowers modeled OH by about 20%.
steps.quote: [...] to approximately 0.3, good agreement between the modeled and observed HO 2 * concentration was achieved

steps.action: Revise the X amount from 0.1 to 0.25 ppb so that OH and HO2* are reproduced together with gamma 0.3 (Fig. S6).
steps.quote: good agreements of OH observations–simulations and HO 2 * observations–simulations were both achieved when the amount of X changed from 0.1 to 0.25 ppb

steps.action: Estimate the ROx primary production and termination rates and channel shares from the base model; they balance at about 4 ppb/h maxima, dominated by photolysis.
steps.quote: P ( RO x ) was dominated by the photolysis reactions

steps.action: Compare the ROx primary production with Heshan, Wangdu, Backgarden, Yufa, Taizhou and Chengdu.
steps.quote: The RO x primary production rate was similar to those at Heshan

steps.action: Compute the AOC from observed OH plus O3 and modeled NO3 (peak 11.8 ppb/h, OH 95.7% in daytime) and compare it with published AOC values (Table 1).
steps.quote: Herein, we explored the AOC in Shenzhen based on the observed radical concentrations for the first time.

steps.action: Bin P(O3)net, AOC from VOCs and their ratio by NO: the ratio rises then falls, with a maximum of about 4.5 near 1 ppb NO.
steps.quote: the maximum of the median ratios existed when NO concentration was approximately 1 ppb

steps.action: Keep the nonlinear NO dependence of ozone yield and draw the control-strategy implication.
steps.quote: it is necessary to optimize the NO x and VOC control strategies for the reduction of O 3 pollution effectively

steps.action: State the headline conclusion: a low-NO missing OH source, explained by X (0.1 ppb, or 0.25 ppb with gamma 0.3), with LIM1 at 7% and MACR/MVK insignificant.
steps.quote: unclassical OH recycling was identified again in this study

end.claim: RACM2-LIM1 underestimates observed OH in the low-NO regime at Shenzhen because of a missing OH source (lower limit up to about 4.6 ppb/h). An NO-independent recycling species X equivalent to 0.1 ppb NO (0.25 ppb with HO2 uptake gamma 0.3) reproduces the observations, while LIM1 explains about 7% and MACR/MVK chemistry contributes nothing significant.

decisive_move.sentence: The OH experimental budget showed a destruction-production gap of 3.1-4.6 ppb/h beyond the combined uncertainties; without it there is no missing source for X, LIM1 or MACR/MVK to explain.

gates.evidence: Action: the campaign was designed for radical closure in the light of earlier missing-OH findings (§1 ¶2-3), but no stated hypothesis directed specific acquisitions. Claim: the OH budget (§4.1 ¶2) could have closed within uncertainties, and LIM1 and MACR/MVK could have explained the gap (§4.2.2 ¶3-4). The X amount and gamma were fitted to the data (§4.2.2 ¶2, §4.3 ¶2), so the X explanation faced no independent test. Registration: only the literature gamma values 0.08 and 0.2 were taken from prior work, and they were applied after the data were seen; nothing was fixed before.

novelty_claims.quote: Herein, we explored the AOC in Shenzhen based on the observed radical concentrations for the first time.

limits: No review file or open discussion was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The headline X explanation is a post hoc fit of a numerical species whose chemical nature is unknown; the paper calls it identified again, but no test could have rejected it (inference). OH interference was not measured in this campaign: the evidence is the group's earlier pre-injector tests, a comparison with Wangdu conditions, and modeled ROOOH, and the authors acknowledge that unmeasured interference might matter. HO2 is reported as HO2*; the RO2 interference (23-28%) is estimated from the model with sensitivities from another campaign, and RO2 was not measured, so HO2 and RO2 budgets could not be closed. Aerosol surface area was approximated as PM2.5 times 20. kOH was measured on only part of the campaign. Sub-claims and their statuses: RO2 interference 23-28% (estimate_with_resolution, model-based, uncertainty not given); missing OH source 3.1-4.6 ppb/h as a lower limit (estimate_with_resolution); gamma about 0.3, which the authors call speculative (estimate_with_resolution, weak); X 0.1-0.25 ppb (estimate_with_resolution, dependent on the gamma choice); ROx budget shares and AOC peak 11.8 ppb/h (estimate_with_resolution, no uncertainty reported); nonlinear P(O3)net/AOC_VOCs dependence on NO with maximum near 1 ppb (regularity_in_range, about 0.1-10 ppb NO, one campaign). The composition is coded trace_series because conditions were found and the claim is the best explanation among rivals; the repeats are days and NO bins within one campaign, not independent traces, so the fit is approximate (inference). The order of analysis outside the published text is not documented.

disagreements.support: Observed OH matches the base model in the high-NO regime but is increasingly underestimated toward low NO, beyond combined uncertainties.
disagreements.quote: a continuously increasing underestimation of the observed OH was found towards lower NO concentrations

disagreements.target: Leuven isoprene mechanism LIM1 as the explanation of missing OH (Peeters et al., 2009, 2014)
disagreements.support: The LIM1 contribution computed against the OH budget explains only about 7% of the missing source.
disagreements.quote: The LIM1 mechanism can explain approximately 7 % of the missing OH sources during 10:00–16:00 CST

disagreements.target: OH regeneration from MACR and MVK oxidation (Fuchs et al., 2014, 2018)
disagreements.support: Model runs with the modified MACR and MVK schemes show no significant contribution in this campaign (Fig. S5).
disagreements.quote: no significant contribution of the MACR and MVK oxidation schemes was found in [...]

disagreements.target: ROOOH as a source of OH interference in FAGE instruments (Fittschen et al., 2019)
disagreements.support: Modeled ROOOH does not correlate with the OH discrepancy here, and the group's Taizhou modulation tests found no significant ROOOH interference.
disagreements.quote: no significant relevance between ROOOH and the underestimation of OH radicals

disagreements.target: HO2 uptake coefficients of 0.08 (Tan et al., 2020, Wangdu) and 0.2 (Li et al., 2018) used in models
disagreements.support: Model runs with these gamma values fail to match observed HO2*; about 0.3 is needed, comparable with gamma measured at Mt. Tai, Mt. Mang, Kyoto and Yokohama.
disagreements.quote: The modeled HO 2 * cannot match well with the observations when a γ value of 0.08 and 0.2 was set in the model.

alternatives_considered.reason: Conversion efficiency reaches 100% in high-NO mode, so the literature RO2 relative sensitivities apply

alternatives_considered.chosen: Modeled kOH for the OH destruction rate
alternatives_considered.reason: kOH was measured only on several days; modeled and measured kOH agree within uncertainty

alternatives_considered.chosen: HO2* concentrations in the OH budget
alternatives_considered.reason: True HO2 could not be calculated without RO2 observations; using HO2* makes the missing source a lower limit

alternatives_considered.alternatives: LIM1 isoprene isomerization; MACR and MVK oxidation schemes; ROOOH/OH measurement interference
alternatives_considered.reason: LIM1 explains about 7%, MACR/MVK nothing significant, ROOOH not correlated; X reproduces OH

alternatives_considered.reason: No direct ASA observations in this campaign
